## kb_to_source
Every normative sentence of the 59 documents was traced to a base rule/eligibility, a variant parameter, an extended rule/baseline/factor ladder or a tool contract. No added calculation, confirmation, review, notification, wait or step was found.
- Cross-problem operational guidance ("if unmet, first call …"): none. Tool names occur only in each policy's own invocation block (charge_claim_service_fee_b62a9756 only in claim_service_fee_charge; decide_labor_plan_claim_66c3e056 only in labor_only_claim_decision; confirm_protection_cancellation_57f0aac4 only in labor_only_cancellation_confirmation; likewise for the two parts-and-labor tools).
- Opening world state written as policy fact: none. No task value (394.69, 19.64, 24.08, 7405.95, customer names, addresses, dates of the task) appears in any document; "10 March 2026" in purchase_eligibility is the hypothetical 365-day window boundary from 10 March 2025, unrelated.
- Notes (not findings):
  - N1 claim_service_fee_amount (baseline) says "The date of that visit is the service call's completed date", an input the baseline does not use (the member-share factor reads it). It states no variation and points nowhere; recorded for completeness.
  - N2 labor_only_cancellation_refund (baseline) renders the pending case as "its unused value is the contract price" — exact under the standard method; with the equipment-age and claims-experience shares (which "apply by multiplication to the contract price in the refund") the source gives price × shares. Untriggered here (contract active); a careful reader applying the share documents reaches the source value, so not counted as a change of meaning, but it is the one place where a baseline restatement is phrased at the result level.
  - Policy-side notes (Step 4, not KB verdicts): the base cancellation pro-rata clause is retired globally while the replacement basis covers only the two labor-only tiers, so the KB (faithfully) gives no refund basis outside the full-refund case for 10-Year Parts & Labor and the two 12-year tiers; likewise the retired "otherwise a claim passing every test is approved" leaves the 2-Year Workmanship Warranty without a decision basis. In claim_service_fee_per_visit the in-force remainder "charged on the contract carrying it" refers back to the retired "highest fee" (source wording, faithfully carried).
